_meta.purpose: Info-button content for Critter Feature. Keyed by critter name (must match critter_roster.json). identity = one short line (what it is + how it fights). funFacts = 2-3 short, real, fact-checked bullets. Missing key => hide the (i).
_meta.batch: 1 of N — active seed-42 decks + canonical starters. Rest of the 127 to follow.
_meta.author: cowork

Tardigrade.identity: The unkillable micro-animal — wins by simply refusing to die.
funFacts: Has survived boiling, freezing, crushing pressure, and the raw vacuum of space.
Can dry into a lifeless 'tun' and revive years later when rehydrated.
Also called the water bear or moss piglet.

Peregrine Falcon.identity: The fastest animal alive — a guided missile with feathers.
funFacts: In a hunting dive (a 'stoop') it exceeds 200 mph, the fastest of any animal.
Special baffles in its nostrils let it breathe at those speeds.
Lives on every continent except Antarctica, including on city skyscrapers.

Hummingbird.identity: A jewel-sized aerial acrobat with a furnace for a heart.
funFacts: The only bird that can fly backwards and hover in place.
Its wings beat so fast they blur into a hum, and its heart can top 1,000 beats per minute.
To survive cold nights it drops into torpor, nearly shutting its body down.

Raccoon.identity: The masked opportunist — clever paws, no shame.
funFacts: Its front paws are so sensitive and dexterous it can open latches and jars.
It often 'washes' or rolls food in water before eating.
One of the most adaptable mammals, thriving in cities as easily as forests.

Golden Snub-Nosed Monkey.identity: A snow-country primate dressed in gold.
funFacts: Lives high in the cold mountain forests of central China.
Its thick golden coat lets it tolerate snow few other monkeys could survive.
Travels in some of the largest troops of any monkey.

Anglerfish.identity: A deep-sea ambusher that fishes with its own glowing lure.
funFacts: The glowing 'lure' on its head is lit by symbiotic bacteria.
In some species the tiny male fuses permanently to the female's body.
It lives in the crushing dark of the deep ocean, far below sunlight.

Dumbo Octopus.identity: The deepest-dwelling octopus — gentle, ghostly, big-eared.
funFacts: Named for the ear-like fins it flaps to swim, like Disney's Dumbo.
Lives deeper than almost any other octopus, thousands of metres down.
Instead of an ink sac it simply drifts away from danger.

Harpy Eagle.identity: The heavyweight raptor of the rainforest canopy.
funFacts: Among the most powerful eagles on Earth, with rear talons the size of a grizzly bear's claws.
It snatches monkeys and sloths straight out of the trees.
It can swivel its head and raise a crown of feathers when alert.

Mata Mata Turtle.identity: A living leaf with a vacuum for a mouth.
funFacts: Its flat, flappy head and shell mimic dead leaves and bark.
It doesn't chew — it snaps its mouth open and sucks prey in with the water.
A long snorkel-like nose lets it breathe without surfacing.

Hippopotamus.identity: A three-ton river tank — one of Africa's deadliest animals.
funFacts: It secretes a red, oily 'blood sweat' that works as sunscreen and antibiotic.
It can't truly swim — it walks and pushes along the river bottom.
Despite a plant diet, it's responsible for many human deaths in Africa each year.

Flying Dragon (Draco).identity: A gliding lizard that sails the forest on rib-wings.
funFacts: It glides on 'wings' made of skin stretched over elongated ribs.
It can sail many metres tree-to-tree, but it cannot truly fly or flap.
Males flash a bright throat-flag to signal and display.

Axolotl.identity: The eternal-baby salamander that grows its body back.
funFacts: It can regrow limbs, organs, and even parts of its brain and heart.
It stays in its larval form for life, keeping its feathery gills.
Critically endangered, it's native only to the ancient lakes of Mexico City.

Poison Dart Frog.identity: A thumbnail of pure warning-colour and venom.
funFacts: Its bright colours warn predators that it's toxic — honest advertising.
It gets its poison from the ants and mites it eats; captive-raised ones aren't toxic.
Indigenous hunters once tipped blow-darts with the toxin of a few species.

Tuatara.identity: A living fossil — the last of an order older than the dinosaurs' fall.
funFacts: It isn't a lizard; it's the sole survivor of an ancient reptile lineage.
It has a light-sensitive 'third eye' on top of its head as a youngster.
It lives slow and long — well over 100 years — in New Zealand.

Sloth.identity: The slowest mammal — and weirdly, a strong swimmer.
funFacts: It moves so slowly that green algae grows in its fur as camouflage.
It climbs down to the ground to relieve itself only about once a week.
It can hold its breath and swim far faster than it ever moves on land.

Hairy (Wolverine) Frog.identity: The 'horror frog' that breaks its own bones into claws.
funFacts: When threatened it snaps its toe bones and pushes them out through the skin as claws.
Breeding males grow hair-like skin strands thought to absorb extra oxygen.
It lives in the forests and streams of Central Africa.

Beaver.identity: Nature's engineer — reshapes whole rivers with its teeth.
funFacts: Its dams create wetlands that countless other species depend on.
Its ever-growing front teeth are coated in iron, giving them an orange tint.
It's the second-largest rodent in the world.

Gorilla.identity: The gentle giant — the largest primate, built like a wrestler.
funFacts: It shares about 98% of its DNA with humans.
Troops are led by a dominant 'silverback' male.
Despite its power it's mostly peaceful and eats a largely plant diet.

Swordfish.identity: A high-speed predator that hunts with a living blade.
funFacts: It slashes through schools of fish with its long, flat bill to stun prey.
It can warm its eyes and brain to see sharply in cold deep water.
It's among the fastest fish in the ocean.

Giant Squid.identity: The deep's great phantom — eyes like dinner plates.
funFacts: It has the largest eyes of any known animal, up to the size of a dinner plate.
It's a favourite prey of the sperm whale, which dives deep to hunt it.
Living ones were filmed in the wild only in the last couple of decades.

Immortal Jellyfish.identity: The creature that cheats death by growing young again.
funFacts: When stressed or aging, it can revert its cells back to its juvenile polyp stage.
In principle this cycle can repeat indefinitely — biologically 'immortal'.
The whole animal is smaller than a fingernail.

Bar-headed Goose.identity: The altitude champion — flies over the roof of the world.
funFacts: It migrates straight over the Himalayas, among the highest-flying birds known.
Its blood and lungs are specially tuned to grab oxygen from thin air.
It can climb to those heights in a matter of hours.

Jaguar.identity: The water-loving big cat with a skull-cracking bite.
funFacts: Pound for pound it has the strongest bite of the big cats — it kills by piercing the skull.
Unlike most cats it loves water and swims readily.
Its name comes from a word meaning 'he who kills in one leap'.

Anaconda.identity: The heavyweight constrictor of the Amazon.
funFacts: The green anaconda is among the heaviest snakes on Earth.
It squeezes prey rather than using venom.
It spends much of its life in slow rivers and swamps, eyes on top of its head.

Tiger.identity: The largest cat — a solitary, striped ambush hunter.
funFacts: Every tiger's stripe pattern is unique, like a fingerprint.
Unusually for a cat, it's a strong and willing swimmer.
It hunts alone, relying on a sudden, explosive ambush.

Saltwater Crocodile.identity: The largest living reptile — patience with a bite like a vice.
funFacts: It has the strongest bite force ever measured in a living animal.
It can cross open ocean between islands, riding currents.
It hunts by waiting, motionless, then exploding from the water.

Sea Otter.identity: A tool-using charmer wrapped in the warmest fur alive.
funFacts: It uses a rock as a tool to crack open shellfish on its chest.
It has the densest fur of any animal — up to a million hairs per square inch.
Otters hold hands while resting so they don't drift apart.

Scorpion.identity: An armoured ancient that glows in the dark.
funFacts: It glows bright blue-green under ultraviolet light, and no one is fully sure why.
Its lineage is over 400 million years old, older than the dinosaurs.
Some species can survive a year or more without eating.

Raven.identity: The feathered genius — a problem-solver in black.
funFacts: It uses tools, plans ahead, and can mimic sounds, including human words.
Ravens play — sliding down snowbanks and tumbling in the air seemingly for fun.
They recognise individual faces and hold grudges.

Polar Bear.identity: The Arctic's apex hunter — a bear built for the ice.
funFacts: Its skin is black and its fur is hollow and clear, not actually white.
It can smell a seal through three feet of packed snow.
It's such a strong swimmer it's classified as a marine mammal.

Black Panther.identity: Not a species — a leopard or jaguar wearing midnight.
funFacts: 'Black panther' just means a big cat with a black coat; its spots are still there under the dark.
The extra pigment may help it hunt unseen at night.
In bright light you can sometimes see the hidden rosettes.

Opossum.identity: North America's marsupial survivor — plays dead to live.
funFacts: When terrified it involuntarily 'plays possum,' going limp and foul-smelling.
It's highly resistant to snake venom and rarely carries rabies.
It eats thousands of ticks in a season.

Platypus.identity: The riddle mammal — it lays eggs and hunts by electricity.
funFacts: It's one of the only mammals that lays eggs.
Its bill senses the faint electric fields of prey underwater, eyes shut.
Males have a venomous spur on each hind leg.

Orca.identity: The ocean's top predator — a dolphin that hunts in packs.
funFacts: It's actually the largest member of the dolphin family.
Different pods have distinct dialects and hunting cultures passed down for generations.
No wild orca is known to have killed a human.

Dolphin.identity: The grinning genius of the sea.
funFacts: It sleeps with half its brain awake so it never stops breathing.
It 'sees' with sound, using echolocation to map its world.
Each dolphin has a signature whistle — effectively a name.

Bald Eagle.identity: America's emblem — a fish-hawk with a seven-foot wingspan.
funFacts: It isn't bald; 'bald' comes from an old word for white-headed.
Its eyesight is roughly four times sharper than a human's.
Its huge stick nests can weigh as much as a small car.

Ant.identity: The tireless soldier — unstoppable in numbers.
funFacts: It can carry many times its own body weight.
Ant colonies behave like a single 'superorganism.'
Ants have farmed fungus and herded aphids for millions of years.

Grizzly Bear.identity: A mountain heavyweight with a shoulder hump of pure muscle.
funFacts: That shoulder hump powers its digging and devastating swipes.
It can sprint faster than a racehorse over short distances.
It eats almost anything, from berries to elk to moths.

Squirrel.identity: The acrobat of the treetops — and an accidental forester.
funFacts: It plants thousands of trees by forgetting where it buried nuts.
Its ankles can rotate so it climbs down headfirst.
It fakes burying food to fool watching thieves.

Armadillo.identity: A little armored tank that can roll up its name.
funFacts: The three-banded armadillo can curl into a sealed ball.
It can hold its breath and walk along the bottom of streams.
Nine-banded armadillos almost always give birth to identical quadruplets.

Great White Shark.identity: The ocean's most famous predator — built around teeth.
funFacts: It can detect a single drop of blood in a huge volume of water.
It loses and replaces thousands of teeth over its life.
It breaches clear out of the water to ambush seals from below.

Barracuda.identity: A torpedo of teeth in the shallows.
funFacts: It strikes in fast, slashing bursts to cut prey in two.
It's drawn to flashes — shiny objects can trigger a strike.
It can hold nearly still, then accelerate explosively.

Vulture.identity: The sky's clean-up crew — death's quiet recycler.
funFacts: Its stomach acid is strong enough to kill anthrax and cholera.
Its bald head stays cleaner when feeding inside carcasses.
It can soar for hours on rising thermals without a wingbeat.

Mosquito.identity: The deadliest animal on Earth — by the diseases it carries.
funFacts: Only the females bite; they need blood to make eggs.
It finds you by the carbon dioxide in your breath.
It kills more people each year than any other animal.

Lion.identity: The team hunter of the savanna — strength in the pride.
funFacts: Lions are the only big cats that live in social groups.
A male's roar can be heard up to five miles away.
Females do most of the hunting, working together.

Inland Taipan.identity: The most venomous land snake alive — and famously shy.
funFacts: A single bite carries enough venom to kill many adult humans.
Despite that, it's reclusive and bites people extremely rarely.
It changes color with the seasons to manage heat.

Brown Recluse.identity: A small, shy spider with a violin on its back and a nasty bite.
funFacts: A dark violin-shaped mark sits behind its eyes.
It has six eyes instead of the usual eight.
It bites only when trapped against skin; most 'recluse bites' are misdiagnoses.

Mountain Goat.identity: The cliff dancer — at home where nothing else can stand.
funFacts: Its soft, rubbery hoof pads grip sheer rock like climbing shoes.
It scales near-vertical cliffs to escape predators.
It isn't a true goat, but a goat-antelope.

Stingray.identity: A flattened, gliding shark-cousin with a barbed tail.
funFacts: It buries in sand and senses prey by their electric fields.
Its tail barb is purely defensive, used only when stepped on.
It 'flies' through water by rippling its wing-like fins.
Its 'horn' is actually a single tooth that can grow nine feet long.
The tusk is packed with nerves and may sense the water around it.
It dives over a mile deep under Arctic ice.

Thorny Devil.identity: A walking pincushion that drinks with its skin.
funFacts: Grooves between its spines wick water straight to its mouth.
It eats thousands of ants in a single meal.
A false 'head' on its neck fools predators.

Mantis Shrimp.identity: A pint-sized boxer with the fastest punch in nature.
funFacts: Its club-strike accelerates like a bullet and can crack aquarium glass.
The punch is so fast it boils the water into imploding bubbles.
Its eyes carry more color receptors than any other known animal.

African Bush Elephant.identity: The largest land animal — a giant with a long memory.
funFacts: Its trunk has tens of thousands of muscles and can pick up a single blade of grass.
It communicates in deep rumbles that travel for miles.
Herds are led by the oldest, wisest female.

White Rhino.identity: A two-ton grazer wearing a horn of hair.
funFacts: Its horn is made of keratin — the same stuff as your fingernails.
'White' is likely a mistranslation of a word meaning 'wide,' for its lip.
It's the second-largest land mammal after the elephant.

Musk Ox.identity: An Ice Age survivor that forms a living fortress.
funFacts: When threatened, the herd circles up, horns out, calves inside.
Its undercoat, qiviut, is warmer than wool and finer than cashmere.
It has roamed the Arctic since the age of mammoths.

Dung Beetle.identity: The strongman recycler that steers by the stars.
funFacts: It can pull over a thousand times its own body weight.
It rolls dung balls in a straight line by navigating with the Milky Way.
It buries waste that would otherwise bury the plains.

Rhinoceros Beetle.identity: A horned tank — one of the strongest creatures for its size.
funFacts: It can lift many times its own body weight relative to its size.
Males joust with their horns over mates.
It's completely harmless to humans despite the fearsome look.

Pistol Shrimp.identity: A shrimp that shoots a stunning bubble-gun.
funFacts: Snapping its claw fires a bubble that stuns prey with a shockwave.
The snap is one of the loudest sounds in the ocean.
The collapsing bubble briefly flashes light and reaches scorching heat.

Coconut Crab.identity: The largest land crab — strong enough to crack a coconut.
funFacts: Its claws grip with a force rivaling a lion's bite.
It climbs trees and can't swim as an adult — it would drown.
It can live for decades and grow a leg-span over three feet.

Water Buffalo.identity: The muscle of the wetlands — a horned heavyweight.
funFacts: It wallows in mud to cool off and shed parasites.
Domesticated buffalo plow fields and feed much of the world.
Wild herds will mob predators as big as tigers.

Chimpanzee.identity: Our closest cousin — a tool-using strategist.
funFacts: It shares around 98% of its DNA with humans.
It makes and uses tools, from termite-fishing sticks to leaf sponges.
Pound for pound it's far stronger than a person.

Octopus.identity: The shape-shifting genius with eight arms and three hearts.
funFacts: Most of its neurons are in its arms, which can act semi-independently.
It can change color and texture in an instant to vanish.
It has three hearts and blue, copper-based blood.

African Grey Parrot.identity: The talking brain of the bird world.
funFacts: It can learn hundreds of words and use them in context.
Some have shown the reasoning of a young child.
It can mimic voices and sounds with eerie accuracy.

Pig.identity: A smart, social omnivore that's cleaner than its reputation.
funFacts: It's widely considered smarter than a dog.
It rolls in mud to cool down, since it can't sweat well.
It has an excellent sense of smell, used to find truffles.

Rat.identity: The ultimate survivor — clever, social, everywhere.
funFacts: It laughs when tickled, in ultrasonic squeaks.
It can squeeze through a gap the size of a quarter.
It shows empathy, freeing trapped cage-mates before taking food.

Orangutan.identity: The thoughtful red ape of the rainforest canopy.
funFacts: It builds a fresh sleeping nest in the trees almost every night.
It uses leaves as gloves, umbrellas, and napkins.
Its name means 'person of the forest.'

Giraffe.identity: The tallest animal — a long-necked browser of the treetops.
funFacts: Its neck has just seven bones, the same number as yours.
Its tongue is dark, nearly black, and around 18 inches long.
It only needs a few minutes of sleep a day.

Hagfish.identity: The slime artist of the deep — a knot-tying scavenger.
funFacts: It can drown an attacker by gushing buckets of slime in seconds.
It ties itself in a knot to scrape that slime off and feed.
It has no jaws and a skull but no spine.

Lungfish.identity: A fish that breathes air and naps through droughts.
funFacts: It gulps air with true lungs and can drown if kept underwater.
It survives dry seasons cocooned in mud for months — even years.
Its lineage stretches back hundreds of millions of years.

Glass Frog.identity: A frog you can almost see through.
funFacts: Its translucent belly reveals its beating heart and organs.
It hides its red blood in its liver while sleeping to stay invisible.
Males guard the eggs on leaves above streams.

Sea Cucumber.identity: The ocean floor's humble recycler with a wild defense.
funFacts: Threatened, it can shoot its own sticky guts at an attacker — and regrow them.
It breathes through its rear end.
It cleans and recycles sediment like an earthworm of the sea.

Bombardier Beetle.identity: A beetle that fires a boiling chemical cannon.
funFacts: It mixes chemicals to blast a near-boiling spray from its rear.
The spray fires in rapid machine-gun pulses.
It can aim the jet in almost any direction.

Aye-Aye.identity: A nocturnal lemur that hunts grubs like a woodpecker.
funFacts: It taps on wood and listens for hollow tunnels with huge ears.
Its long, skeletal middle finger hooks grubs out of the bark.
It's the world's largest nocturnal primate.

Tarsier.identity: A tiny primate that is mostly eyes.
funFacts: Each eyeball is bigger than its brain.
It can't move its eyes, so it swivels its head almost all the way around.
It can leap many times its body length between trees.

Maned Wolf.identity: The 'fox on stilts' of the South American grasslands.
funFacts: It isn't a wolf or a fox, but its own unique canid.
Its very long legs help it see over tall grass.
Its scent-marking smells startlingly like cannabis.

Blobfish.identity: The deep-sea 'ugliest animal' — but only at the surface.
funFacts: At its home depth, pressure gives it a normal fish shape.
It looks like a sad blob only because decompression ruins it.
It barely moves, drifting just above the seafloor to feed.

Pink Fairy Armadillo.identity: The smallest armadillo — a rose-shelled sand swimmer.
funFacts: It's barely the size of a hand and almost never seen.
It 'swims' through loose desert sand and burrows in seconds.
Its pink shell flushes with blood to release heat.

Star-Nosed Mole.identity: A blind burrower with the fastest snack reflex on Earth.
funFacts: Its 22 fleshy nose-tentacles are the most sensitive touch organ known.
It identifies and eats prey in under a quarter of a second.
It can smell underwater by blowing and re-inhaling bubbles.

Hoatzin.identity: The 'stinkbird' — a leaf-eater that ferments like a cow.
funFacts: It digests leaves by fermentation, giving it a manure-like smell.
Its chicks are born with claws on their wings to climb.
It's an evolutionary oddball with no close living relatives.

Goblin Shark.identity: The deep-sea 'living fossil' with jaws that shoot out to grab prey.
funFacts: Its jaws fling forward off its face to snatch prey, then retract.
Its pink color comes from blood vessels showing through translucent skin.
Its lineage goes back roughly 125 million years.

Pangolin.identity: The walking pinecone — the only mammal clad in scales.
funFacts: It rolls into an armored ball so tight even lions give up.
Its sticky tongue can be longer than its body.
It's the most trafficked mammal in the world.

Earthworm.identity: The silent engineer that builds the soil.
funFacts: It eats its way through earth, enriching it as it goes.
If cut, it can sometimes regrow its tail end.
Charles Darwin spent decades studying its role in making fertile land.

Termite.identity: The tiny architect — builder of skyscraper mounds.
funFacts: Its mounds use natural air-conditioning that inspires human buildings.
Colonies can number in the millions around a single queen.
It digests wood with the help of microbes in its gut.

Spectral Bat.identity: The Americas' largest bat — a carnivore of the night.
funFacts: It hunts birds, rodents, and even other bats.
Its wingspan can approach a metre across.
Pairs are unusually devoted, often roosting as a family.

Whale Shark.identity: The largest fish alive — a gentle, spotted giant.
funFacts: It can grow longer than a school bus yet eats tiny plankton.
Each one's pattern of spots is unique, like a fingerprint.
It filters thousands of litres of water an hour to feed.

Manta Ray.identity: The graceful giant of the open water — a flying filter.
funFacts: Its 'wings' can span more than 20 feet.
It has the largest brain of any fish and may recognise itself in mirrors.
It does barrel-roll somersaults to feed on plankton clouds.

Box Jellyfish.identity: A near-invisible drifter with among the deadliest venom.
funFacts: Its sting is one of the most potent in the animal kingdom.
Unlike most jellyfish, it has clusters of true eyes and swims actively.
Its bell is cube-shaped, giving it its name.

Blue Dragon (Glaucus).identity: A thumbnail sea slug that steals its prey's weapons.
funFacts: It eats the venomous Portuguese man o' war and stores the stingers.
It floats upside-down on the surface tension of the sea.
Its concentrated stolen venom can pack a stronger sting than its prey's.

Vampire Squid.identity: A deep-sea phantom that lives on falling 'snow.'
funFacts: It isn't a true squid or octopus, but its own ancient lineage.
It eats 'marine snow' — drifting bits of dead matter.
Threatened, it turns its cloak of arms inside-out over itself.

Harp Sponge.identity: A deep-sea sponge that turned predator.
funFacts: Unlike most sponges, it traps and digests tiny animals.
Its harp-like branches are covered in velcro-like hooks.
It was only discovered in the deep ocean in recent years.

Komodo Dragon.identity: The largest lizard — a venomous ambush giant.
funFacts: It can take down prey as large as water buffalo.
Its bite delivers venom that prevents blood from clotting.
Females can sometimes reproduce without a male.
It can shape itself to imitate sea snakes, lionfish, and flatfish.
It picks which animal to mimic based on the threat nearby.
It was only discovered by science in the 1990s.

Kakapo.identity: The world's heaviest parrot — flightless, nocturnal, and rare.
funFacts: It can't fly; it climbs trees and 'parachutes' down.
Males boom like a bass drum all night to attract mates.
Only a couple hundred survive, each with a name.

Superb Bird-of-Paradise.identity: A showman that transforms into a dancing smiley-face.
funFacts: The male spreads his feathers into a black oval with two bright 'eyes.'
He snaps and dances for a famously hard-to-impress female.
His black plumage is among the darkest material in nature.

Ostrich.identity: The biggest bird alive — it gave up flight for speed.
funFacts: It can sprint over 40 mph and outrun most predators.
Its eye is bigger than its brain.
A single kick can be powerful enough to kill a lion.

Fossa.identity: Madagascar's top predator — part cat, part mongoose.
funFacts: It's the island's largest carnivore and hunts lemurs through the trees.
It can climb down trunks headfirst like a squirrel.
It's more closely related to the mongoose than to cats.

Capybara.identity: The world's largest rodent — unbothered and beloved.
funFacts: It's the size of a big dog and totally at home in water.
It's so easygoing that other animals lounge on top of it.
It lives in chilled-out social herds near rivers.

Quokka.identity: The 'happiest animal' — a smiling little marsupial.
funFacts: Its facial shape makes it look permanently cheerful.
It's famous for posing in tourists' selfies.
It lives mainly on a few islands off Western Australia.

Hyrax.identity: A guinea-pig-sized animal whose closest cousin is the elephant.
funFacts: Despite the looks, it's related to elephants and manatees.
It has tiny tusks, like miniature elephant ivory.
It basks in the sun for hours because it regulates heat poorly.
It's the giraffe's only living relative, with a shorter neck.
Its striped legs help it vanish in dappled jungle light.
It was unknown to outside science until the 1900s.

Red Panda.identity: A fire-colored bamboo-eater that's a panda in name only.
funFacts: It belongs to its own family, not the bear or raccoon line.
It has a false 'thumb' to grip bamboo.
It wraps its bushy tail around itself like a blanket.

Markhor Goat.identity: The screw-horned wild goat of the high crags.
funFacts: Its corkscrew horns can grow over five feet long.
It scales sheer Himalayan cliffs with ease.
It's the national animal of Pakistan.

Raccoon Dog (Tanuki).identity: A masked canid that naps through winter.
funFacts: It's a true dog relative that just looks like a raccoon.
It's the only canid that enters winter torpor, a light hibernation.
It's a legendary shapeshifter in Japanese folklore.

Velvet Worm.identity: A living fossil that hunts with a slime cannon.
funFacts: It shoots jets of sticky slime to glue prey in place.
It has barely changed in hundreds of millions of years.
It walks on rows of soft, stubby leg-nubs.

Colugo.identity: The most graceful gliding mammal in the trees.
funFacts: A membrane stretches from neck to tail-tip, even between its toes.
It can glide the length of a football field between trees.
Despite the nickname 'flying lemur,' it neither flies nor is a lemur.

Rakali (Water Rat).identity: Australia's native otter-rat — a riverbank hunter.
funFacts: It has webbed hind feet and a waterproof coat.
It learned to flip toxic cane toads to eat only the safe parts.
It hunts fish, frogs, and even small birds.

Ghost Bat.identity: Australia's only carnivorous bat — a pale night hunter.
funFacts: It wraps prey in its wings and bites the skull.
Its pale, semi-transparent wings give it a ghostly look.
It hunts birds, frogs, and other bats.

Patagonian Mara.identity: A long-legged rodent that lives like a tiny deer.
funFacts: It bounds and stots across the plains like an antelope.
It's one of the largest rodents in the world.
Pairs mate for life — rare among rodents.

Emperor Tamarin.identity: A tiny monkey with a magnificent white mustache.
funFacts: Its sweeping white whiskers reportedly recall a German emperor.
It's small enough to sit in your hand.
Groups stay in touch with bird-like trills.

Siphonophore.identity: Not one animal but a colony living as one — and possibly the longest creature alive.
funFacts: It's made of many specialized bodies working together as a single being.
One deep-sea giant was measured longer than a blue whale.
The Portuguese man o' war is a siphonophore, not a jellyfish.

Jewel Wasp.identity: The zombie-maker — a wasp that turns roaches into puppets.
funFacts: Its sting flips a precise switch in a cockroach's brain.
The dazed roach then walks obediently to the wasp's burrow.
Its larva grows up inside the still-living host.

Human (Male).identity: The endurance generalist — a brain that builds tools and tells stories.
funFacts: Humans are among the best long-distance runners in the animal world.
We can throw fast and accurately better than any other species.
Our oversized brains let us cooperate in groups of millions.

Human (Female).identity: The endurance generalist — a brain that builds tools and tells stories.
funFacts: Humans are among the best long-distance runners in the animal world.
Language lets us pool knowledge across generations.
Our species reshaped nearly every ecosystem on Earth.

Nautilus.identity: A living fossil cephalopod that jets through the deep in a coiled shell.
funFacts: It has drifted the oceans almost unchanged for hundreds of millions of years.
It moves by jet propulsion, squirting water from a tube.
Its spiral shell is divided into gas-filled buoyancy chambers.

Cicada.identity: The patient screamer — years underground for weeks in the sun.
funFacts: Some broods spend 13 or 17 years underground before emerging together.
The males are among the loudest insects on Earth.
They emerge in such huge numbers that predators simply can't eat them all.
It can flash shifting patterns across its skin in a heartbeat.
It's likely colorblind yet matches colors perfectly — perhaps by sensing polarized light.
Its pupils are a strange W shape.

Wood Frog.identity: The frog that freezes solid and lives.
funFacts: In winter its heart stops and most of its body turns to ice.
It floods its cells with natural antifreeze to survive.
Come spring, it thaws and hops away as if nothing happened.

Naked Mole Rat.identity: A wrinkled underground oddball that barely ages.
funFacts: It lives in bee-like colonies ruled by a single breeding queen.
It almost never gets cancer and feels no sting from acid.
It can survive long stretches with almost no oxygen.

Orb-Weaver Spider.identity: The patient engineer of the dew-jeweled web.
funFacts: It often rebuilds its entire wheel-shaped web every night.
Its silk is, for its weight, tougher than steel.
It senses prey through vibrations in the threads.

Horseshoe Crab.identity: A 450-million-year-old living fossil with blue blood.
funFacts: Its blue blood is used to test medicines for contamination.
It's more closely related to spiders than to crabs.
It has survived essentially unchanged since before the dinosaurs.

Peacock Spider.identity: A grain-of-rice spider that dances in neon.
funFacts: The male lifts a vivid, patterned flap and dances to court a mate.
It's only a few millimetres long.
A poor performance can get the suitor eaten.

AI.identity: The newcomer in the bracket — intelligence without a body.
funFacts: It has no muscles, claws, or venom — only pattern and prediction.
Its 'reach' is whatever tools and machines it can direct.
In this arena it's the wildcard: powerful in mind, fragile in the flesh.

Arctic Tern.identity: The migration champion — it chases endless summer pole to pole.
funFacts: It flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year.
Over a lifetime its travels can equal several trips to the Moon.
It sees more daylight than any other animal.

Wandering Albatross.identity: The widest wings in the world — a tireless ocean glider.
funFacts: Its wingspan can exceed 11 feet, the largest of any living bird.
It can glide for hours, even sleep on the wing, without flapping.
It may circle the entire Southern Ocean in a single journey.

Common Swift.identity: The bird that lives in the air.
funFacts: It can stay airborne for months at a time without landing.
It eats, sleeps, and even mates on the wing.
Its feet are so small it can barely walk on the ground.

Emperor Penguin.identity: The Antarctic endurance king — it breeds in the cruelest winter.
funFacts: Males balance the egg on their feet through months of polar dark.
It dives deeper and longer than any other bird.
Colonies huddle and rotate so everyone shares the warm center.

Slime Mold.identity: A brainless blob that solves mazes — the ultimate underdog.
funFacts: It has no brain or nerves yet finds the shortest path through a maze.
It can recreate efficient transport networks like a city's rail map.
It's neither plant, animal, nor fungus — a category of its own.
